theory.overview: Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) delivers equivalent security to RSA and DH with dramatically smaller keys—256-bit ECC provides ~3072-bit RSA security. This efficiency makes ECC ideal for mobile devices, IoT, and high-throughput systems. Bitcoin, Ethereum, TLS 1.3, and modern secure messaging rely on ECC. Understanding elliptic curves requires grasping the discrete logarithm problem in elliptic curve groups—a different mathematical foundation than integer factorization.

sections.title: Elliptic Curves
sections.content: Elliptic curves are defined by equations like y² = x³ + ax + b over finite fields. Points on the curve form a group under point addition: given points P and Q, draw a line through them, find the third intersection with the curve, and reflect across the x-axis to get P+Q. Scalar multiplication—adding a point to itself k times—is the core operation: Q = k*P. This is fast to compute but reversing it (finding k given P and Q) is the Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem (ECDLP), which is computationally infeasible for well-chosen curves.
keyPoints: Curve equation: y² = x³ + ax + b

sections.title: ECDH and ECDSA
sections.content: ECDH (Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman) follows the same logic as DH but uses elliptic curve scalar multiplication. Alice and Bob exchange public keys Q_A = d_A*G and Q_B = d_B*G, then compute shared secret S = d_A*Q_B = d_B*Q_A = d_A*d_B*G. ECDSA signatures: choose random k, compute R = k*G, r = R_x mod n, s = k⁻¹(h + r*d) mod n. Signature is (r, s). Bitcoin uses ECDSA with secp256k1 curve.
keyPoints: ECDH: Shared secret from scalar multiplication
ECDSA: Sign with private key, verify with public

sections.title: Standard Curves
sections.content: NIST curves (P-256, P-384, P-521) are widely used but have controversial origins (NSA-designed). Curve25519 (by DJB) is faster, safer, and designed transparently—no suspicious constants. Ed25519 provides EdDSA signatures. secp256k1 (used by Bitcoin) has no known weaknesses but is less widely supported. When choosing curves: prefer Curve25519 for new systems, use NIST curves for compliance, avoid obsolete curves below 256 bits.

practiceProblems.title: ECC Key Size
practiceProblems.description: What RSA key size provides equivalent security to 256-bit ECC?

solution.explanation: 256-bit ECC provides approximately 128-bit security, equivalent to 3072-bit RSA. This is why ECC is preferred for resource-constrained devices.

practiceProblems.title: ECDLP vs DLP
practiceProblems.description: Why is ECDLP harder than integer discrete logarithm?

solution.answer: No sub-exponential algorithms known for ECDLP
solution.explanation: While integer DLP has sub-exponential algorithms (Number Field Sieve), no such algorithms are known for ECDLP. The best attacks are exponential Pollard's rho.

snippets.title: ECDH with Python
snippets.code:
from Crypto.PublicKey import ECC

# Generate key pairs
alice_key = ECC.generate(curve='P-256')
bob_key = ECC.generate(curve='P-256')

# Shared secret
alice_secret = alice_key.d * bob_key.pointQ
bob_secret = bob_key.d * alice_key.pointQ
